Marissa / Karthik — reviewed Helix's redlines. Summary and proposed approach below.

Summary of risk: Helix is asking to prohibit use of any Customer Content for training/improvements. That is negotiable, but we need a tight definition that: (a) protects customer-identifiable content (PHI/PII/records), and (b) allows Redwood to operate and improve the service (bug fixes, model calibration) under safe telemetry and limited aggregate/anonymous metrics.

Proposed counter-language (high-level):
- Define "Customer Content" as any data or content submitted by customer that is reasonably identifiable to the customer or its users.
- Add a "Model Training and Improvement" section: Redwood will not use Customer Content to train, fine-tune, or derive model weights for general-purpose models or make such content available to third-party model development partners, except: (i) with Customer's prior written consent; or (ii) for aggregate, de-identified telemetry that cannot be reasonably re-identified and that is used solely to evaluate service performance and reliability.
- Telemetry carve: specify examples (latency, error rates, token counts, hashed request IDs) and explicitly exclude request payloads/outputs from the allowed telemetry.
- Subprocessors: commit to providing a pre-approved list and 30-day notice for new subprocessors; maintain SCCs for EU transfers and offer on-prem options if needed.

Attachment: Redwood_proposed_training_clause.docx contains the verbatim text. My suggestion: send the counter-language inline to Helix and propose a single DocuSign envelope for execution (keeps turnaround small). If Helix still insists on an absolute ban, escalate to execs for credit/contract tradeoffs.

-Neha

Hi Samantha — thanks for the redline and for the quick turnaround. Our legal team proposes the following counter-language (verbatim below) to address Helix's concerns while preserving the operational telemetry we need to run the service: 

--- Proposed clause (for insertion into Section 3.x):

"Model Training and Improvement. 

1) Definitions: 
"Customer Content" means any data, text, or other content submitted to Redwood by or on behalf of Customer in connection with the Services, that is reasonably identifiable to Customer or its end users.

2) Training Use Prohibition: 
Redwood will not use Customer Content to train, fine-tune, or derive weights for models that are made available to other customers or the public, nor will Redwood provide Customer Content to third-party model developers for such purposes, without Customer's prior written consent.

3) Permitted Operational Telemetry: 
Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood may collect and process aggregate, de-identified telemetry and service metrics (e.g., latency distributions, error rates, token volume, hashed request identifiers) solely for the purposes of service performance monitoring, debugging, and reliability improvements, provided that such telemetry does not include request payloads or generated outputs, and cannot be reasonably re-identified to Customer or any individual.

---

If that aligns with Helix's expectations we can put a single DocuSign envelope together and circulate for signature. DocuSign envelope: https://www.docusign.com/envelope/00A1B2C3D4E5 (prepped for Helix + Redwood). HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/7321.
